"The predictability of a user's future posts based on their past posts (as measured by perplexity) is a reliable indicator of their privacy risk on a forum, with users below a certain perplexity threshold being identifiable from anonymized posts." Calibrated MoE under distribution shift: maybe "Forums with dynamic expert assignment (like MoE) for moderation tasks will maintain higher moderation accuracy when topic distributions shift (e.g., from technical to political discussions) compared to a single monolithic moderator." But we need a cross-domain transfer linking "forum" and "memory". So memory is a cognitive/machine learning concept. The materials mention MemoryWAM (persistent memory for world action modeling). So "Applying MemoryWAM's persistent memory architecture to model user behavior in a forum will yield better prediction of thread participation and next post content than traditional Markov models." Alternatively, the forum itself as a memory system: "Structuring a forum as an external memory for a language model, using read/write operations similar to MemoryWAM, will enable the LM to answer questions about past discussions with higher accuracy than retrieval-augmented generation with a static index."
